## Summary 

Agenda formation + two mechanisms of profit-motivated influence 

1. Structure Is Destiny for agenda formation (also partisanship)

2.  Structure Is Destiny for in-house science. Our lack of transparency is bad. It empowers deep-pocketed industry. 

3. Expensive taste-making lawyers legitimize interpretations of fact and law.

. . . 

Agreement that the **norms of science** can help. Tension over the structural role of **scientists** in decision-making.



# Dwidar and Richardson:<br> "Who Makes the Rules?" {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".2"}

## Summary of Findings 1:  **HUGE** partisan conflict effects {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

Officials reporting **high** partisan conflict over their agencies

- More perceived influence of appointees
- Less perceived influence of career staff

## Summary of Findings 2:  **CONDITIONAL** partisan conflict effects {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

Officials reporting **high** partisan conflict over **liberal agencies**

- More perceived influence of appointees

Officials reporting **low** partisan conflict over **conservative agencies** 

- More perceived influence of career staff

. . .

[Does this depend on who the president is? ]()

## Summary of Findings 3: {background-image="https://i.pinimg.com/originals/53/88/62/538862d56741248fc085109b93946efb.png" background-opacity=".1"}

### Insulated agencies 

- Less perceived influence of president/OMB/OIRA

### Expertise + uncertainty 

- Less perceived influence of appointees, Congress, the president, and OMB/OIRA when their agency's work requires skill and policy effects are uncertain

# Wagner:<br> "How Not to Design Expert Bureaucracy" {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".3"}


## **Argument:** Corruption pervades in an unequal society {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}


Agencies face asymmetric pressure regarding who participates, who raises technical challenges, and who sues

Despite saying they support scientific integrity, appointees:

- manage peer review with partisan goals, including selecting reviewers, advisory panels, questions, and timing
- most often advocate on behalf of industry 

Courts make it worse.

- Exhaustion Doctrine compounds advantages of industry
- Threat of litigation pressures agencies to preemptively capitulate to industry-friendly facts 
- Hard look focuses on substance, often factual judgment, not process 
   - "process integrity is effectively irrelevant to courts, so agencies focus their limited resources instead on anticipating and defending against technical critiques mounted by regulated industry." 
   - Uncritically treat rigged advisory boards as reliable, rewarding panel stacking and manipulation




## The call to Agencies {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

(in hopes of deference or safe harbor)

1. clarify the line between empirical and normative judgments
1. explain why their record is reliable
1. be transparent 

## The call to Congress {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

1. Revise APA: "arbitrary or capricious, **including with respect to the scientific integrity of the factual record.**" 
     -  ideally, also a safe harbor for documentation of their work <!--(as if they had not disclosed it?) -->
1. Revise  (b)(5): open factual record to FOIA
1. New process requirements for explanation, peer review, and transparency that are not judicially reviewable but may contribute to arbitrary and capricious review. 

## The call to Courts {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

1. Look suspiciously upon science that involves only industry 
1. Revise exhaustion doctrine & encourage diverse interveners
1. Reverse expansion of (b)(5) FOIA exemptions




## {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

**Premise:** Evidence-based policy is a bipartisan political goal.^[Political in the sense that it shifts power, hopefully away from regulated industry.]

## Restatement  

Goal 1: Insulate agency scientists

- how? By requiring agencies to explain and document why their work can be trusted
 
Goal 2: Increase oversight from diverse reviewers and public interest groups while decreasing industry influence 
 
- how? Be more suspicious of industry participation. Make records more cheaply available. 

## Is NEPA reform a model? {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

> "102(2)(D) ensure the professional integrity, including scientific integrity, of the discussion and analysis in an environmental document." 

- Building United States Infrastructure through Limited Delays and Efficient Reviews Act of 2023

[Or is it evidence that industry sees an opportunity to add a cause of action?]() 

## Other challenges to overcome {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1"}

1. Relies on the shadow of judicial review
    - downstream of executives' desire to make particular policies
    - only a real threat to a small number of policies
1. Relies on courts to understand scientific conventions (redistricting, climate, 😬)
1.  Description implies prescription 

## Conditional on presidential priorities {visibility="uncounted"}

A more unitary executive ***could*** use tools of conflict disclosure, peer review, and process transparency to improve the reliability of information.


| | science is convenient | science is inconvenient |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| Outcomes | compatible |  compatible? | 
| Perceptions| compatible | incomptatable |



Yet, these are not consistent across issues and time. Without systemic reform, a president can reap the benefits of both non-interference and interference. 

> "He would relinquish valuable opportunities to control the scientific record with few corresponding benefits."

> "Executive interference in fact-finding appears to benefit predominantly if not exclusively, regulated industry." 



. . .

But, mainly, Wagner is calling for constraints on presidential control.

## Questions for an unequal world {background-image="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/EDp03OAWkAE36Sl?format=jpg" background-opacity=".1" .incremental}

[**Assuming process reforms are somewhat sticky, do they frustrate or enable counter-scientific pressure? **]()

::: {.incremental}

1. **Conflicts of interest**: Insulation depends on the strength of norms. Could be co-opted. 

2. **Peer review**: Likely positive, but tradeoffs: allows opponents to expunge new science (as in the EPA transparency rule)

3. **Transparency** (e.g., fewer (b)(5) exemptions): Tradeoffs. Clarifies influences (if observers have capacity) and reduces costs of technical comments, but also gives ammunition to hostile groups.

:::

# Libgober:<br>  "Legitimacy Brokers" {background-image="https://www.abajournal.com/images/main_images/shutterstock_white_shoes.jpg" background-size="cover" background-opacity=".2"}

> "Council to the situation"---White-Shoed God-Guru-Influencers for Hire in Regulatory Lobbying

## Gems 💎

- The Language Broker simile: McDonald's & Home Depot as "displaced corporate persons" in the foreign terrain of Dodd-Frank lobbying

- ABA ethics rules prohibit "polycliental situationships” (DOJ is in such a situationship with all the agencies)


## Why hire white shoes?  {background-image="https://www.abajournal.com/images/main_images/shutterstock_white_shoes.jpg" background-size="cover" background-opacity=".2"}

- Lawyers: **Litigation proofing**

- Political scientists: **Subsidy** (also revolving door, access, influence networks)

- Sociologists: **Bridging social networks** (e.g., revolving door)

- Libgober (JD/PhD): **Legitimacy brokering** (***laundering?***) 

(not mutually exclusive, depends on agency)

. . . 

Important! **Mechanisms** of ***cultural capture***.



## Clarifying the mechanisms  {background-image="https://www.abajournal.com/images/main_images/shutterstock_white_shoes.jpg" background-size="cover" background-opacity=".2"}


1. Intermediary/"honest broker"/"wider view" --> ***understanding*** (translating and situating)
1. Fixer --> ***deals*** (brokering)
     - Adjust the conflicts = innovation: "how one can do things"
1. Blame avoidance (p. 18)
1. Credible signaling (p. 19)
1. Deploy reputational and cultural capital

## Social movemnts and corporate brand  { visibility="uncounted"}

I think there is something to this surprise mechanism, but when I tried to test it against the alternative “legibility” hypothesis that those most familiar with the justice frame, not those to whom it would be surprising, were more likely to adopt it and change rule language. However, I also found that when this occurs, the policy is more likely to move, so I think the novelty is doing some work, just conditional on legibility. Happy to talk more about this. 

Attracting attention + fear of attention (p. 17) - Fire alarms are half the story. Happy to talk more about this.

Don't dismiss firms' brand management efforts. They might not always be as successful as they would like, but they are not widely boycotted. This type of PR is not what brokers typically do, but it does not mean that firms never do it. 

However, this all seems quite tangential to your intervention. As it stands, it is a lengthy digression, but in my opinion, not long enough to properly address public moral reputation management. 

## Structure  { visibility="uncounted"}

There are many digressions. You do a decent job of bringing the reader along with things like "returning to ...". Still. I think you want to 

1. set them apart with subheadings 
2. ask what role each serves and make sure it is tightly accomplishing that task
